title: Concerts Are Inspiring Travel Across Asia
paragraphs: For many music fans in Asia, a concert is not just a night out. It can also be a reason to travel to another country.

In November 2026, the travel company Trip.com Group and the concert company Live Nation Asia released a report called "The Concert Travel Effect in Asia." For the report, they surveyed 1,768 people in six places: Singapore, mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, Thailand and South Korea.

The report found that 65% of the concertgoers had traveled to another country or region to see a concert. Seven in 10 fans said live music was one of the most exciting reasons to travel. Fans said that the perfect concert trip lasts about four days. In addition, 63% said they chose five-star hotels when they traveled for concerts.

Many fans are also interested in buying concert tickets and travel together. In the survey, 84% said they were interested in packages that include both. Trip.com and Live Nation Asia have worked together since 2025, and bookings for their packages grew 64% in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier.

Big concerts can cause sudden increases in travel. For example, after tickets went on sale early for a BTS concert tour, flight bookings from Hong Kong to Bangkok rose 309% in three days. And within a day of early ticket sales for concerts by The Weeknd, flight bookings to Singapore rose 203%.
In Singapore, 45% of people surveyed had traveled abroad for a concert. South Korea was their favorite place to travel for concerts.
James Dick of Live Nation Asia said that a concert "can make a city feel like somewhere a fan needs to be." He also said that "One show can set a whole journey in motion."
However, the numbers come from the companies' own research, which has not been checked by independent experts.
